brief.headline: Fix the 40% return rate first, then push price toward ₹0.65–0.80/pc at volume

priceAsk.summary: Target ₹0.65–0.80/pc for induction-wad caps at higher volume
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asking prices for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps sit at ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc. The verdict is MARKET-FAIR but notes modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — our target sits in that band.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 days after receipt; no extension until return rate drops

brief.financialLeverage: Scorpion publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit, or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.66 L annual spend is tiny — we have almost no size leverage here. The real pressure point is quality: 40% of their deliveries come back, which burns their margin and our time. Fix that first, then use the threat of moving volume to Manjushree Technopack (₹2569.83 Cr rigid-plastic giant) or Mold-Tek (₹1010.97 Cr listed leader) to justify the price ask.

evidence.point: 40% of deliveries are returned or reversed
Our annual spend with them is only ₹1.66 lakh
Market asking price for 28 mm induction-wad PP caps is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typically ₹0.85–0.95/pc
Market verdict shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec
evidence.figure: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health score B 65/100) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) covering pails, containers, pharma — robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited (market lead)
alternates.why: Pan-India manufacturer lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — a potential maker-direct option for resin or finished goods

risks: The 40% return rate signals quality or paperwork problems — pushing too hard on price before they fix that may make service even worse
Our ₹1.66 L spend is so small they may not care if we walk; we need alternates lined up to make the threat real
No public financials means we're flying blind on their stability — if they fold or exit the line, we have no warning
Moving to a big alternate like Manjushree may mean higher MOQs or longer lead times — qualify their terms before the meeting
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We need to talk about the 40% return rate — it's costing both of us — and then see where we can land on price if we grow volume and tighten the loop.
